sections.name: limiter
sections.title: Per-address event limit and recording
sections.what: Allows 120 events per minute per address, then records the event with the signed-in user id and returns its id.
sections.why: Likely reason: the limit is per address because visitors who are not signed in also send events.
sections.watch_out: The cast to the property type skips a type check, so the event schema is the only real guard.

summary: Records events sent from the browser, such as opening a receipt, along with the signed-in user if there is one.
purpose: Keeps a record of how fans use the app, to measure it.
why: The comment says client events are recorded on the server with the session's user id, so the browser cannot forge the user.
how: 1) Checks the per-address limit. 2) Checks the event body. 3) Records the event with the signed-in user id if there is one. 4) Returns the new event id with status 201.
inputs: A POST with an event name and its properties. The user comes from the session.
outputs: A JSON event id with status 201.
risks: Properties are cast to the expected type after the body check, so a mismatch between the check and the type could slip through.
debug: If events are missing, check the limit and the body shape in the analytics types, then the track function in the analytics service.
